[element-month]
=== `<month>` Month (in a citation)

Names one of the months of the year, such as “`July`” or “`07`”.

#### Related Elements

Dates within the metadata of a standard do not use this element. Within citations (<<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>> and <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>>), this element is used to name the month of publication. The elements <<element-year,`<year>`>>, <<element-date,`<date>`>>, <<element-day,`<day>`>>, <<element-month,`<month>`>>, and <<element-season,`<season>`>> may all be used to describe the date a cited resource was published. Other dates inside a citation, such as a copyright date, the date on which the author accessed the resource, or a withdrawal date, should be tagged using <<element-date-in-citation,`<date-in-citation>`>> with the <<attribute-content-type,`@content-type`>> attribute used to name the type of date (`copyright`, `access-date`, `time-stamp`, etc.).
